works.title: Tears of Steel

works.summary: In a post-apocalyptic Amsterdam dome, scientists and soldiers attempt to replay a pivotal memory to prevent robotic extinction.

works.title: Big Buck Bunny

works.summary: A gentle giant rabbit outwits three woodland bullies using inventive slapstick traps across a sunlit meadow.

works.title: Elephants Dream

works.title: Cosmos Laundromat

works.title: Spring

works.summary: A young shepherdess and her dog confront ancient towering forest spirits to usher in the cycle of seasons.

works.title: Metropolis

works.title: Nosferatu

works.title: Night of the Living Dead

works.title: His Girl Friday

works.title: Charade

works.summary: In wintry Paris, a young widow is pursued by wartime conspirators searching for a stolen fortune hidden in plain sight.

works.title: The General

works.title: Sherlock Jr.

works.title: Stalker

works.title: Solaris

works.title: Detour

works.title: Carnival of Souls

works.title: D.O.A.

works.title: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari

works.title: A Trip to the Moon

works.summary: Astronomers launched from a giant cannon land right in the eye of the Moon and encounter acrobatic Selenites.

works.title: The Stranger
works.creator: Orson Welles
works.summary: A war-crimes investigator tracks a fugitive Nazi mastermind hiding behind antique clockwork in a quiet Connecticut town.

works.title: My Man Godfrey
works.creator: Gregory La Cava
works.summary: A Depression-era ‘forgotten man’ hired as butler to an eccentric Manhattan socialite family quietly outsmarts them all.

works.title: Plan 9 from Outer Space

works.summary: Cardboard tombstones and hubcap flying saucers collide as aliens resurrect corpses to halt humanity's solarbonite weapon.

works.title: Gymnopédie No. 1 (Lent et douloureux)
works.creator: Erik Satie · Kevin MacLeod (CC BY)
works.summary: Sparse suspended major-seventh piano chords floating in quiet nocturnal stillness, precursor to modern ambient minimalism.

works.title: Goldberg Variations, BWV 988: Aria
works.creator: Johann Sebastian Bach · Kimiko Ishizaka (CC0)
works.summary: Luminous ornamented sarabande on modern piano recorded under CC0 public dedication with crystalline voice-leading.

works.title: Clair de Lune (Suite bergamasque)
works.creator: Claude Debussy · Laurens Goedhart (CC BY)
works.summary: Rippling impressionist arpeggios in D-flat major evoking moonlight on still water.

works.title: Cello Suite No. 1 in G Major, Prelude
works.creator: Johann Sebastian Bach · John Michel (CC BY-SA)
works.summary: Unbroken resonant cello arpeggios climbing steadily with warm wooden harmonics and focused momentum.

works.title: The Planets, Op. 32: I. Mars, the Bringer of War
works.creator: Gustav Holst · US Air Force Band (PD)
works.summary: Relentless asymmetric 5/4 ostinato and low brass stomp that directly birthed heavy film scoring and metal riffs.

works.title: Romeo and Juliet, Op. 64: Dance of the Knights
works.creator: Sergei Prokofiev
works.summary: Crushing low-string march and jagged brass stabs with sub-bass weight worthy of modern hip-hop production.

works.title: Recomposed: Vivaldi Four Seasons – Spring 1
works.creator: Max Richter
works.summary: Baroque solo violin motifs rewired over subterranean modular synth sub-bass and hypnotic loop repetition.

works.title: The Four Seasons, Summer: Presto
works.creator: Antonio Vivaldi · John Harrison (CC BY-SA)
works.summary: Relentless minor-key string storm and blazing sixteenth-note violin sweeps at pure punk tempo.

works.title: Koyaanisqatsi
works.creator: Philip Glass
works.summary: Monolithic pipe-organ bass pedals and chanting arpeggios engineered like pure trance architecture.

works.title: Gnossienne No. 1 (Lent)
works.creator: Erik Satie · Public Domain
works.summary: Hypnotic minor-mode piano vamp with smoky chromatic ornaments that sounds ready-made for lo-fi beats.

works.title: Night on Bald Mountain
works.creator: Modest Mussorgsky · Skidmore Orchestra (PD)
works.summary: Slashing string tremolo and thunderous brass fanfares erupting from subterranean gloom.

works.title: Music for 18 Musicians: Pulses
works.creator: Steve Reich
works.summary: Breathing bass clarinets, marimbas, pianos, and wordless voices cycling through eleven shimmering harmonic centres.

works.title: 1/1 (Music for Airports)
works.creator: Brian Eno
works.summary: Incommensurable acoustic piano and warm synth tape loops drifting gently in and out of phase for contemplative space.

works.title: Xtal
works.creator: Aphex Twin
works.summary: Hazy VHS-warm breakbeats cushioned by ethereal vocal pads and nostalgic analogue synth melodies.

works.title: Roygbiv
works.creator: Boards of Canada
works.summary: Wobbly SH-101 bassline and detuned public-broadcast synth nostalgia over crisp hip-hop pocket drums.

works.title: Hallogallo
works.creator: NEU!
works.summary: Ten minutes of hypnotic 4/4 motorik drum propulsion beneath gliding overdubbed guitar drones on an endless autobahn.

works.title: Autobahn
works.creator: Kraftwerk
works.summary: Minimoog Doppler car horns, vocoder refrains, and sleek electronic percussion mapping modernist highway travel.

works.title: Disorder
works.creator: Joy Division
works.summary: High-neck melodic bassline, clipped snare machine urgency, and stark alienation produced by Martin Hannett.

works.title: Once in a Lifetime
works.creator: Talking Heads
works.summary: Poly-rhythmic Eno-produced Afrobeat groove beneath preacher-cadence existential monologue and glassy chorus swells.

works.title: Blue Monday
works.creator: New Order
works.summary: Oberheim DMX sixteenth-note bass drum burst, sequenced octave synth bass, and deadpan Manchester dancefloor melancholy.

works.title: Everything in Its Right Place
works.creator: Radiohead
works.summary: Prophet-5 five-beat electric-piano pulse and fragmented Kaoss Pad vocal loops dissolving rock into electronic paranoia.

works.title: So What
works.creator: Miles Davis
works.summary: Double-bass call answered by two-chord Dorian horn voicings and unhurried trumpet phrasing on Kind of Blue.

works.title: In a Silent Way
works.creator: Miles Davis
works.summary: Floating dual electric pianos, clean guitar shimmer, and Teo Macero tape-spliced ambient groove — pure late-night headphones.

works.title: Générique (Ascenseur pour l'échafaud)
works.creator: Miles Davis
works.summary: Late-night muted trumpet improvised live to French noir footage over brushed snare and solitary walking bass.

works.title: Time Moves Slow
works.creator: BADBADNOTGOOD · Sam Herring
works.summary: Dusty live-kit pocket, warm analog keys, and smoky jazz chord changes wired straight into modern hip-hop swing.

works.title: Chameleon
works.creator: Herbie Hancock
works.summary: Rubber ARP Odyssey synth bassline and Clavinet pocket that laid the blueprint for West Coast funk and G-funk.

works.title: Haitian Fight Song
works.creator: Charles Mingus
works.summary: Furious bowed-and-plucked upright bass riff that erupts like an acoustic punk anthem.

works.title: Acid Jazz (Extended Rhodes Mix)
works.creator: Kevin MacLeod (CC BY)
works.summary: Tight head-nodding breakbeat drums paired with warm Rhodes electric piano and punchy horn stabs.

works.title: Night on the Docks (Sax Noir)
works.creator: Kevin MacLeod (CC BY)
works.summary: Rainy midnight walking upright bass, brushed ride cymbal, and breathy tenor saxophone without clutter.

works.title: Naima
works.creator: John Coltrane
works.summary: Luminous pedal-point tenor saxophone hymn suspended over rich quartal piano harmonies.

works.title: Teardrop
works.creator: Massive Attack
works.summary: Heartbeat vinyl kick drum, harpsichord figure, and Elizabeth Fraser's soaring crystalline voice in Bristol nocturnal dub.

works.title: Archangel
works.creator: Burial
works.summary: Rain-crackle 2-step shuffles, pitched R&B vocal ghosts, and South London night-bus sub-bass.

works.title: Windowlicker
works.creator: Aphex Twin
works.summary: Elastic micro-edited breakbeats, vocoded sighs, and blown-out sub-bass distortion climax.

works.title: Breathe
works.creator: The Prodigy
works.summary: Whip-crack snare breaks, surf-punk guitar snarl, and relentless arena rave adrenaline.

works.title: N.Y. State of Mind
works.creator: Nas
works.summary: DJ Premier upright-bass loop and menacing piano stabs driving razor-sharp Queensbridge street reportage.

works.title: Accordion
works.creator: Madvillain
works.summary: Madlib's wheezing Daedelus accordion sample looping endlessly under MF DOOM's dense internal rhyme schemes.

works.title: Pink Moon
works.creator: Nick Drake
works.summary: Intimate close-miked alternate-tuning acoustic guitar, hushed baritone voice, and a single brief piano cascade.

works.title: Avril 14th
works.creator: Aphex Twin
works.summary: Delicate mechanical Disklavier miniature whose felt hammers click softly through a wistful two-minute melody.

works.title: Biochem: acetyl-CoA
works.creator: Cohort Open · biochem
works.summary: Pyruvate dehydrogenase processing yields a two-carbon unit that enters the citric acid cycle. What is that product called? — OpenStax names the pyruvate-derived compound acetyl CoA.

works.title: Biochem: allosteric regulation
works.creator: Cohort Open · biochem
works.summary: An allosteric inhibitor typically binds where on the enzyme? — OpenStax describes an allosteric site that still prevents substrate binding at the active site.

works.title: Biostats: probability
works.creator: Cohort Open · biostats
works.summary:
In a study model, event X has probability 0.20 and event Y has probability 0.30. The model explicitly assumes the two events are independent.

Which of the following probabilities should it assign to both events occurring in the same participant? — For independent events, the joint probability is the product of their individual probabilities. Multiplying 0.20 by 0.30 gives 0.06, or a 6% chance of both.

works.title: Biostats: hypothesis testing
works.creator: Cohort Open · biostats
works.summary:
A trial compares the mean change in a measurement between a new intervention and a control. The planned statistical test evaluates whether the population means differ.

Which of the following statements is the null hypothesis for this comparison? — For this comparison, the null hypothesis states that the two population mean changes are equal. A difference of zero expresses that no-difference claim on the measurement scale.

works.title: Cardiovascular: ABO blood group
works.creator: Cohort Open · cardiovascular
works.summary:
A 50-year-old woman with type A blood inadvertently receives type B blood during surgery. Within minutes she develops fever, flank pain, and hypotension, and the transfusion is stopped immediately.

Which of the following best explains why this reaction began — In contrast to antibodies against the Rh antigen, which are produced only after exposure, ABO group antibodies are preformed, so a type A recipient already carries anti-B antibodies that react immediately with donor B ce

works.title: Cardiovascular: electrocardiogram
works.creator: Cohort Open · cardiovascular
works.summary: A 24-year-old medical student reviewing a normal ECG tracing identifies distinct deflections corresponding to atrial depolarization, ventricular depolarization, and ventricular repolarization, but cannot find any deflection corresponding to atrial repolarizati — Atrial repolarization occurs at about the same time as ventricular depolarization, and its small signal is masked by the much larger QRS complex.

works.title: Endocrine: hemoglobin A1C
works.creator: Cohort Open · endocrine
works.summary:
A patient with diabetes has an A1C value measured during a routine visit.

The laboratory value most directly quantifies which molecular event? — Sustained blood glucose exposure increases glycation of hemoglobin within circulating red cells.

works.title: Endocrine: hemoglobin A1C
works.creator: Cohort Open · endocrine
works.summary: A 52-year-old's daily glucose readings improved during the past week, but today's A1C remains elevated. Which of the following interpretations best reflects what this test measures? — The cited passage states that A1C measures glucose-attached hemoglobin and reflects average blood glucose over the past three months.

works.title: Epidemiology: attributable risk
works.creator: Cohort Open · epidemiology
works.summary: The attributable proportion (attributable risk percent) is primarily a measure of what? — CDC defines the attributable proportion, also called the attributable risk percent, as a measure of the public health impact of a causative factor.

works.title: Epidemiology: case-fatality
works.creator: Cohort Open · epidemiology
works.summary: A health department reports the case-fatality rate for an infectious disease. Which of the following does this measure express? — CDC defines the case-fatality rate as the proportion of persons with a particular condition (cases) who die from that condition.

works.title: Gastrointestinal: gastrointestinal
works.creator: Cohort Open · gastrointestinal
works.summary:
An investigator collects a chief-cell secretion containing an inactive protein-digesting precursor. Adding a second aliquot of the same secretion does not restore digestion. Acidification permits activation, after which protein cleavage is detected.

Which of — The available precursor becomes functional when acidification permits activation. This distinguishes an activation defect from failed secretion or insufficient precursor.

works.title: Gastrointestinal: gastrointestinal
works.creator: Cohort Open · gastrointestinal
works.summary:
A gastric mucosal preparation retains its mucus layer and intact epithelial tight junctions. A selective intervention removes bicarbonate from the mucus without changing acid secretion into the lumen.

Which of the following protective functions is most direct — Bicarbonate neutralizes acid within the mucus. Removing it reduces chemical protection even when mucus thickness and epithelial junctions are preserved.

works.title: Genetics: autosomal recessive inheritance
works.creator: Cohort Open · genetics
works.summary: Two unaffected parents are each known carriers of the same pathogenic variant for an autosomal recessive disorder. What is the probability that their next child will inherit the disorder? — An Aa by Aa cross yields AA, Aa, Aa, and aa in equal quarter-probabilities; only aa is affected.

works.title: Genetics: genetics
works.creator: Cohort Open · genetics
works.summary:
A child has a completely penetrant autosomal recessive disorder. Sequencing identifies two distinct pathogenic variants in the same gene. One was inherited from the mother and one from the father. Neither parent is affected.

Which of the following best descri — Each parent contributed a different pathogenic allele at the same locus. Both copies are affected, satisfying the recessive model through compound heterozygosity rather than identical variants.

works.title: Hematology: hematology
works.creator: Cohort Open · hematology
works.summary:
Two hypothetical anemia models are compared. In model X, erythrocyte destruction is measured to exceed replacement. In model Y, the marrow fails to produce adequate blood cells.

Which of the following best distinguishes the primary mechanisms? — X matches the definition of hemolytic anemia: destruction exceeds replacement. Y identifies the production failure described by aplastic anemia, separating the two mechanisms despite their shared outcome.

works.title: Hematology: hematology
works.creator: Cohort Open · hematology
works.summary: A hypothetical intestinal transport experiment supplies adequate vitamin B12 and functional intrinsic factor directly to the intestinal contents. Uptake remains markedly reduced after a specific distal small-intestinal segment is removed. There is no vitamin b — B12 absorption occurs in the terminal ileum. Adequate vitamin and functional intrinsic factor cannot restore uptake when the relevant intestinal compartment itself has been removed.

works.title: Immunology: immunology
works.creator: Cohort Open · immunology
works.summary:
A purified bacterial capsular polysaccharide vaccine produces an inadequate response in a target pediatric population. A redesigned vaccine chemically links the same polysaccharide to a protein carrier.

Which of the following is the principal purpose of addin — Adding the carrier changes polysaccharide immunity from a T-cell-independent pattern to a T-cell-dependent one, allowing more durable protection.

works.title: Immunology: immunology
works.creator: Cohort Open · immunology
works.summary: In a hypothetical experiment, two otherwise comparable samples receive a live attenuated viral vaccine. One sample contains antigen-matched circulating antibodies shown to interfere with the vaccine organism; the other does not. The antibody-containing sample — Live attenuated organisms replicate to produce their vaccine response. Antibodies that interfere with this step can reduce the resulting active response in the exposed sample.

works.title: Microbiology: microbiology
works.creator: Cohort Open · microbiology
works.summary: A hypothetical cholinergic-terminal assay compares two otherwise identical preparations exposed to botulinum neurotoxin. In preparation X, a release-associated protein can be cleaved. In preparation Y, the same protein retains normal function but resists cleav — The susceptible preparation loses function when its release protein is cleaved. Preserving that protein despite equal toxin entry should protect transmitter output in the resistant preparation.

works.title: Microbiology: microbiology
works.creator: Cohort Open · microbiology
works.summary:
A 46-year-old patient remains conscious while developing symmetric flaccid weakness that begins with cranial-nerve findings and progresses downward.

Which of the following cellular changes best connects the toxin's action with this pattern of impaired motor f — Botulinum neurotoxin disrupts release-associated proteins at cholinergic terminals. The resulting reduction in acetylcholine output links the cellular lesion to descending flaccid motor impairment.

works.title: Musculoskeletal: musculoskeletal
works.creator: Cohort Open · musculoskeletal
works.summary:
Developing skeletal tissue initially contains a hyaline cartilage model. Follow-up sections show removal of that template and deposition of bone in its place.

Which of the following interpretations best describes the process observed? — Endochondral ossification replaces a pre-existing hyaline cartilage model with bone. Removal of the template followed by bone deposition is the defining sequence in this preparation.

works.title: Musculoskeletal: musculoskeletal
works.creator: Cohort Open · musculoskeletal
works.summary:
A volunteer changes from a short maximal effort to prolonged activity at a sustainable intensity. Oxygen delivery remains adequate during the prolonged phase.

Which of the following changes in the relative contribution of energy sources is most consistent wit — Aerobic metabolism sustains ATP production when oxygen is available. Its relative contribution grows as the initial rapid energy stores cannot sustain the activity alone.

works.title: Neuro: neuro
works.creator: Cohort Open · neuro
works.summary:
An action potential reaches a presynaptic terminal normally. A selective blocker prevents opening of the terminal's voltage-gated calcium channels.

Which of the following paired changes is most directly expected after stimulation? — Presynaptic calcium entry triggers vesicle fusion. Preventing that entry reduces the calcium signal and therefore transmitter exocytosis despite arrival of the action potential.

works.title: Neuro: neuro
works.creator: Cohort Open · neuro
works.summary:
Tracer is applied to sensory fibers entering the right side of the spinal cord. Fibers in one pathway cross near entry, whereas those in another remain on the right until reaching the medulla.

Which of the following pairings correctly identifies the modalitie — Temperature fibers use the spinothalamic pathway and cross near spinal entry. Proprioceptive fibers ascend ipsilaterally in the dorsal column before crossing in the medulla, matching both observations.

works.title: Pharmacology: acetaminophen
works.creator: Cohort Open · pharmacology
works.summary: A key safety limit emphasized for acetaminophen from all sources is which daily maximum? — MedlinePlus: do not take more than 4000 mg of acetaminophen per day from all sources.

works.title: Pharmacology: acetaminophen
works.creator: Cohort Open · pharmacology
works.summary:
A patient combines extra-strength acetaminophen with a cold remedy whose label also lists acetaminophen and consequently takes too much of the drug.

Which of the following injuries is directly identified by the cited warning? — The cited warning states that excessive acetaminophen can damage the liver severely enough to require transplantation or cause death.

works.title: Physiology: anemia
works.creator: Cohort Open · physiology
works.summary: Anemia is best defined as which change in red blood cells? — Anemia is a lower-than-normal amount of healthy red blood cells, so the body gets too little oxygen-rich blood; low production, destruction or blood loss can cause it.

works.title: Physiology: asthma
works.creator: Cohort Open · physiology
works.summary: In asthma, what happens to the airways at times? — In asthma the airways can become inflamed and narrowed at times, which makes it harder for air to flow out when breathing out.

works.title: Psych: amygdala
works.creator: Cohort Open · psych
works.summary: Which statement about the amygdala and memory is correct? — The amygdala is involved in fear and in fear memories, linking emotional arousal to what is remembered.

works.title: Psych: classical conditioning
works.creator: Cohort Open · psych
works.summary: Classical conditioning is a process by which organisms learn to do what? — Classical conditioning is learning to associate stimuli and, as a result, to anticipate events, as when a tone comes to predict food.

works.title: Renal: renal
works.creator: Cohort Open · renal
works.summary:
Investigators follow glucose from tubular fluid through a renal epithelial cell into the interstitium. At the luminal membrane, glucose entry is coupled to sodium entry. At the opposite membrane, glucose exits by facilitated diffusion.

Which of the following — Sodium-coupled glucose entry uses the sodium gradient at the apical membrane. Glucose then leaves across the basal membrane by facilitated diffusion into the interstitium.

works.title: Renal: renal
works.creator: Cohort Open · renal
works.summary:
Cultured renal tubular cells have intact apical sodium-glucose symporters. An experimental inhibitor selectively blocks the basal Na+/K+ ATPase. As the intracellular sodium concentration rises, apical glucose uptake falls.

Which of the following best explains — The basal pump keeps intracellular sodium low, maintaining the gradient used for apical sodium entry. Its inhibition dissipates that gradient and indirectly reduces coupled glucose uptake.

works.title: Reproductive: reproductive
works.creator: Cohort Open · reproductive
works.summary:
A 26-year-old patient is studied during the preovulatory portion of a menstrual cycle. Follicular estrogen production is lower than in the comparison cycle.

Which of the following endometrial changes would most directly reflect loss of this hormonal stimulus? — Follicular estrogen stimulates endometrial rebuilding. Reducing that stimulus most directly reduces preovulatory proliferation rather than advancing the postovulatory secretory phase.

works.title: Reproductive: reproductive
works.creator: Cohort Open · reproductive
works.summary:
A postpartum patient has milk within the mammary alveoli. Suckling produces an appropriate rise in circulating oxytocin, but the surrounding myoepithelial cells fail to contract.

Which of the following steps is most directly impaired? — Oxytocin normally drives myoepithelial contraction, which ejects milk from alveoli. The reported lack of contraction localizes the failure to that response.

works.title: Respiratory: Bohr effect
works.creator: Cohort Open · respiratory
works.summary:
During vigorous exercise, a 25-year-old man's active skeletal muscle produces increased amounts of carbon dioxide and lactic acid. Compared with resting muscle, oxygen release from hemoglobin within the exercising muscle's capillaries is enhanced.

Which of th — Carbon dioxide conversion and lactic acid lower local pH; a lower, more acidic pH promotes oxygen dissociation from hemoglobin, delivering more oxygen to the active tissue.

works.title: Respiratory: Boyle's law
works.creator: Cohort Open · respiratory
works.summary:
In a physiology laboratory, a 21-year-old student compresses a gas-filled syringe to one-half of its original volume while temperature is held constant and no gas escapes.

According to Boyle's law, which of the following best describes the resulting change in — Boyle's law states that the pressure of a gas is inversely proportional to its volume at constant temperature: if volume decreases to one-half, pressure increases twofold.

works.title: The free-energy principle: a unified brain theory?

works.summary: Synthesizes perception, action, attention, and learning as minimization of variational free-energy surprise under a generative model.
works.subject: Active Inference

works.title: Active Inference: A Process Theory
works.creator: Karl Friston; Thomas FitzGerald; Francesco Rigoli; Philipp Schwartenbeck; Giovanni Pezzulo
works.summary: Derives neuronal message passing and epistemic action selection from expected free energy over discrete partially observable Markov decision processes.
works.subject: Active Inference

works.title: The theory of constructed emotion: an active inference account of interoception and categorization
works.creator: Lisa Feldman Barrett
works.summary: Accounts for affect and emotion concepts as allostatic predictive regulation of the internal milieu via Bayesian active inference.

works.title: Predictions not commands: active inference in the motor system
works.creator: Rick A. Adams; Stewart Shipp; Karl J. Friston
works.summary: Reframes descending corticospinal projections as proprioceptive predictions resolved by spinal reflex arcs rather than motor commands.
